'''TC-14''' was a [[TC-series protocol droid/Legends|TC-series protocol droid]] with [[Gender/Legends|feminine programming]] stationed aboard the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class battleship]] [[Saak'ak/Legends|''Saak'ak'']].

==Biography==
{{Quote|What? What did you say?''"<br />"''The ambassadors are Jedi Knights, I believe.|Nute Gunray and TC-14|audio=Gunray-TC-14-JediKnights.flac|<ref name="Episode 1" />}}
[[File:Tc-142.jpg|thumb|left|180px|TC-14 aboard the Saak'ak]]
TC-14 was a [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica]] TC-series [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]], part of a special lengthy production run that introduced new features and skill-sets. The company wanted to highlight the introduction of the [[TranLang III communications module/Legends|TranLang III communications module]] center into their [[Droid/Legends|droid]] line by including the letters TC in the serial numbers of all droids produced in this series. Of these, the early ones (including TC-14) were often referred to by a TC prefix. Like TC-14 herself, nearly all of them were programmed with a feminine personality, and like her, they were excellent at operating calmly under pressure. This can largely be attributed to the frequent number of [[Memory wipe/Legends|memory wipes]] she received.

TC-14 was purchased by the Trade Federation and ended up on the ''Lucrehulk''-class battleship ''Profiteer'' (''Saak'ak'') during the Federation's occupation of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. Her etiquette skills proved to be of excellent use to the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidians]] when seeking to distract "problematic" envoys.

It was she who greeted the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] ambassadors (secretly [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and his [[Padawan/Legends|apprentice]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]) during the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|blockade of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. However, she suspected that the ambassadors were none other than [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]].

[[File:Force_Sense_TPM.png|thumb|right|250px|TC-14's attempt to distract the Jedi failed.]]
She reported to Neimoidians [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]], [[Rune Haako/Legends|Rune Haako]], and [[Daultay Dofine/Legends|Daultay Dofine]] that the ambassadors were [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]], which prompted them to send her to delay and distract the Jedi (mostly because Dofine was unwilling to meet the Jedi face to face, despite Gunray needing the Jedi to be occupied while he contacted [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]]). While she served the Jedi drinks, [[Dioxis/Legends|poisonous gas]] filled the room and took them by surprise. As this occurred, TC-14 offered an apology to the ambassadors. After escaping the room, the Jedi spared TC-14 and allowed her to leave.

TC-14's regularly scheduled memory wipe was planned to be brought forward to hide any evidence of the attempted murders from the Senate. She was later stationed on the [[Vuutun Palaa/Legends|''Vuutun Palaa'']] during the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]], and was destroyed along with all crewmembers when [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] blew up the ship.<ref name="Fact File" />

==Behind the scenes==
TC-14 was played by [[John Fensom]] in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']], but the voice of TC-14 was provided by [[Lindsay Duncan]]. In ''The Phantom Menace'' video game TC-14 is voiced by [[Carolyn Seymour]].
